reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended Closing a gzip/deflate dataset can race with an active read because the decompressor is closed before the HTTP body without synchronizing with the read.
1 open issue - [Synchronize decompressor cleanup with active reads](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4548668089) · New
What changed in this PR Addresses #359 by making iterative query dataset closure close the underlying response reader, so stalled reads can be interrupted without cancelling the original request. **Changes:** - Retains the frame reader and closes it from `IterativeDataset.Close()`. - Uses `sync.Once` to prevent repeated underlying close calls. - Adds a regression test for stalled-read interruption and single-close behavior. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `azkustodata/​query/​v2/​iterative_dataset.go` | Connects dataset closure to response-reader cleanup. | | `azkustodata/​query/​v2/​iterative_dataset_close_test.go` | Tests stalled reads and repeated closure. | | `azkustodata/​query/​v2/​frame_reader.go` | Makes reader closure idempotent and preserves its error. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: Closing a gzip/deflate dataset while `advance()` is reading can race inside the decompressor: `response.originalCloser.Close()` closes it before the HTTP body. `sync.Once` only serializes close calls, not reads. Make the wrapper close the HTTP body first, synchronize decompressor cleanup with completion of the active read, and add compressed-response race coverage.
